items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the inference of fault drawn where an accident is of a kind that does not ordinarily happen without carelessness”
o: Standard of care
Professional standard
Res ipsa loquitur
Cost of precautions
items.s: Res ipsa loquitur is the inference of fault drawn where an accident is of a kind that does not ordinarily happen without carelessness.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Pure economic loss?

financial detriment unconnected with any injury to person or damage to property
a recognised mental illness suffered as a result of another's careless conduct
the breach of a legal duty to take reasonable care which causes damage to another

items.q: The correct meaning of Professional standard is

the conduct expected of an ordinary skilled member of a profession exercising that art
failure to reach the standard of care that the law requires in the circumstances
the seriousness of the potential harm, which raises the level of care demanded
items.s: Professional standard: the conduct expected of an ordinary skilled member of a profession exercising that art. The other options describe Magnitude of risk, Standard of care, Breach of duty.

items.q: In this course, Claimant refers to

the party who brings a civil action seeking a remedy for a wrong done to them
the person who commits a civil wrong and thereby becomes liable to answer for it
a court order requiring a party to stop a course of conduct or to do a stated act
items.s: Claimant: the party who brings a civil action seeking a remedy for a wrong done to them. The other options describe Tortfeasor, Injunction, Tort.

items.q: In this course, Fair comment refers to
o: the defence that the statement complained of is substantially true
a defamatory meaning that arises from facts known to the readers rather than the words themselves
the defence that the statement was an honest opinion on a matter of public interest
communication of the defamatory matter to a person other than the one defamed
items.s: Fair comment: the defence that the statement was an honest opinion on a matter of public interest. The other options describe Justification, Publication, Innuendo.

items.q: Strict liability may be defined as

a civil wrong independent of contract for which the injured party may claim compensation
the sum of money awarded by a court to compensate a claimant for a wrong
responsibility imposed for harm regardless of whether the party was at fault
items.s: Strict liability: responsibility imposed for harm regardless of whether the party was at fault. The other options describe Damages, Tort, Claimant.

the inference of fault drawn where an accident is of a kind that does not ordinarily happen without carelessness
the expense and practicality of guarding against a risk, weighed against the likelihood of harm
failure to reach the standard of care that the law requires in the circumstances
items.s: Res ipsa loquitur: the inference of fault drawn where an accident is of a kind that does not ordinarily happen without carelessness. The other options describe Reasonable person, Breach of duty, Cost of precautions.

Libel

the rule that a person must take care to avoid acts likely to injure those closely and directly affected by them
a recognised mental illness suffered as a result of another's careless conduct
the closeness of relationship between the parties, in time, space or dealing, required before a duty arises
